title: SERVING ENVIRONMENT DECISION & DEPLOYMENT PROFILE
verdict_explanation: A fully free profile cannot host the complete assistant (retrieval + BGE-M3 encoding + Qwen3-8B generation) at zero recurring cost on any examined provider. A persistent RETRIEVAL-ONLY profile is viable on Oracle Cloud Always Free Ampere A1 (2 OCPU / 12 GB Arm VM): BM25 + dense index + BGE-M3 query encoding fit within RAM and disk, and an always-on API is possible. Qwen3-8B generation is NOT feasible there (8B model on Arm CPU is impractically slow for interactive use; no free always-on GPU exists on any examined profile). The recommended profile is therefore retrieval-only; generation remains a separate, unresolved gate. This is explicitly NOT a complete AI assistant deployment.
next_action: User provisions an Oracle Cloud Always Free account and one VM.Standard.A1.Flex instance (2 OCPU / 12 GB) in their home region (manual step; requires card verification; NOT done by this task). Then run the Task-78 validation plan (experiments/task78/task78_validate_plan.md) to measure BGE-M3 encoder latency and end-to-end retrieval latency in that environment before any latency gate is claimed passed.

architecture_audit.summary: The repository implements an offline/batch retrieval pipeline with a production BM25 path (H1) and an opt-in hybrid candidate (H3_RRF20). There is NO inference/serving code for answer generation, NO API server, and NO frontend. Answer generation exists only as training configuration (DAPT-01 / SFT-01 for Qwen3-8B-Base); the Task-69/70 RAG answers were produced offline on external GPU sessions and stored as artifacts.

boundaries.notes: Dense index sha-verified (corpus_emb f16 sha f54919e6..., alignment: corpus_text/doc_ids/queries shas + 164238/47 counts). Frozen bench sha 06625f72....

Service does NOT bundle the encoder; callers pass a query_encoder callable or pre-computed embeddings. Encoder model: BAAI/bge-m3 rev 5617a9f..., dim 1024, L2-normalised. Corpus encoding was a one-time Colab T4 job (1882.6 s).
Fusion optimised in Task-77 (~1.3x, exact equivalence proven on 54 cases); contract violations 0 in benchmarks.

components: experiments/task70/retrieval_stack.py (reads pre-computed Task-69 answers; does NOT generate)
boundaries.notes: NO inference/serving code exists. Qwen3-8B-Base + DAPT-01 adapter lineage is training-only. Generation latency and memory are UNRESOLVED and unmeasured.
NONE exists. No FastAPI/flask/gradio/streamlit/uvicorn server anywhere in src/ or experiments/.

resource_requirements.notes: Task-77 measurements are from a 2-physical-core x86 VM without the encoder in the loop. Oracle Ampere A1 Arm cores differ; all latency gates remain UNRESOLVED until measured there.

A_oracle_always_free_ampere.what_runs_free: VM.Standard.A1.Flex up to 2 OCPU + 12 GB RAM (Arm), OR up to 2 VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro AMD instances; 200 GB always-free block volume storage.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.persistent_storage: YES - block volumes persist across stops/starts (200 GB free).
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.cpu_memory: 2 OCPU (Arm Neoverse-N1) + 12 GB RAM total, flexibly allocated across 1-2 instances.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.always_on_api: YES - it is a VM; any long-lived process (e.g., systemd service) can run continuously.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.sleep_suspension: No automatic sleep, BUT idle Always Free instances (CPU/network/memory 95th-percentile < 20% over 7 days) MAY be reclaimed by Oracle.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.capacity_quota: Always Free shapes are capacity-limited per region; 'out of host capacity' errors are possible. One free account per person.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.account_verification: Requires credit/debit card (credit-card logo, no PIN) for identity verification; temporary authorization hold possible; card NOT charged unless upgrading. Mobile number often required.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.charges_possible: Only if Always Free limits are exceeded or non-free resources are provisioned. Staying within Always Free = 0 INR recurring.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.bge_m3_suitability: PLAUSIBLE but UNMEASURED - 12 GB RAM fits model (~2.2 GB) + retrieval (~2.1 GB) with headroom; Arm CPU query-encoding latency unknown (needs validation).
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.dense_retrieval_suitability: YES - dense index (321 MB disk, ~1.3 GB loaded) + numpy search fits easily.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.qwen_generation_suitability: NO for interactive use - Qwen3-8B-4bit (~5.5 GB weights + KV cache) fits tightly in 12 GB alongside retrieval, but Arm CPU generation throughput (~1-3 tok/s class) is impractical for an interactive assistant. No GPU available.
A_oracle_always_free_ampere.terms_to_verify: Home-region choice is permanent for Always Free provisioning; idle-reclamation policy; regional capacity at sign-up time.

D_google_cloud_free_tier.what_runs_free: Always Free: 1 non-preemptible e2-micro VM (shared 0.25 vCPU, 1 GB RAM) in us-west1/us-central1/us-east1; 30 GB persistent disk; 5 GB Cloud Storage; Cloud Run / Cloud Functions request quotas. Plus $300 trial credit for 90 days (NOT sustainable zero-cost evidence).
D_google_cloud_free_tier.persistent_storage: YES - 30 GB persistent disk (e2-micro) + 5 GB Cloud Storage.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.cpu_memory: e2-micro: ~0.25 vCPU shared, 1 GB RAM - far too small for BGE-M3 (~2.2 GB model) or the retrieval stack (~2.1 GB RSS).
D_google_cloud_free_tier.gpu: NOT included in free tier; GPUs always billed.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.always_on_api: e2-micro can run a service, but lacks the memory for this workload. Cloud Run free tier is request-based and scale-to-zero (cold starts).
D_google_cloud_free_tier.sleep_suspension: e2-micro is non-preemptible and always-on within quota; Cloud Run scales to zero.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.capacity_quota: 1 e2-micro per month (by time); region-restricted to 3 US regions.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.account_verification: Billing account with payment method required even for free tier / trial.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.charges_possible: Yes if limits exceeded or non-free resources used; trial credit expiry does not auto-charge but upgrade does.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.bge_m3_suitability: NO - 1 GB RAM cannot load the model.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.dense_retrieval_suitability: NO - retrieval stack RSS (~2.1 GB) exceeds e2-micro RAM.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.qwen_generation_suitability: NO - no free GPU; CPU far too small.
D_google_cloud_free_tier.verdict: Rejected for this workload. e2-micro is an order of magnitude too small.

recommended_profile.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free - Ampere A1 retrieval service
recommended_profile.storage: Boot volume >= 47 GB (min) - enough for corpus (~0.5 GB), dense index (~0.3 GB), OS, and Python env; block volume persists.
recommended_profile.software: Python 3.11+, numpy; sentence-transformers + torch (CPU) for BGE-M3 query encoding; the existing svk_corpus retrieval service.
recommended_profile.service_shape: Long-lived Python process (systemd) exposing RetrievalService.search over a minimal local HTTP endpoint (to be built in a FUTURE task - does not exist yet). BM25 default; hybrid_rrf20 opt-in via SVK_RETRIEVAL_MODE.
recommended_profile.serves: RETRIEVAL ONLY (BM25 + optional H3_RRF20 dense fusion + BGE-M3 query encoding).
recommended_profile.does_not_serve: Answer generation (Qwen3-8B). No frontend. This is explicitly NOT a complete AI assistant.

recommended_controls: Oracle: set a budget/alarm alert in the Console (though Always Free usage should remain 0 INR); do NOT upgrade the account; avoid provisioning any non-'Always Free-eligible' shapes.
Oracle: monitor the idle-reclamation status; a keep-alive workload (e.g., periodic retrieval self-test) can keep utilization above 20% if desired, but must itself stay within free limits.
General: treat any 'out of host capacity' or quota error as a signal to stop, not to upgrade.
cost_billing_safeguards.caveat: Billing alerts and spending caps are safeguards, NOT substitutes for selecting genuinely free resources. If a candidate cannot reliably remain at 0 INR, it is rejected or marked conditional.

validation_plan.prerequisite: Oracle Always Free account + one A1.Flex instance provisioned by the user (NOT by this task).
measurements: Model + encoder initialization time (load BAAI/bge-m3 rev 5617a9f...).
Encoder cold and warm latency (p50/p95/p99) over the frozen 47 queries + repeat workload.
Full answer-generation latency and peak memory (only if/when an inference path exists - currently UNRESOLVED).
Disk usage, cold start, restart behavior.
validation_plan.integrity: Use the verified BGE-M3 revision and Task-74 index; do not download a different model or rebuild verified artifacts without a documented reason. Preserve the frozen benchmark and all existing integrity checks.
validation_plan.gate_claiming: No latency gate is claimed passed until measured in the selected representative environment. Encoder or generator gates that cannot be run remain UNRESOLVED.

risks: Oracle A1 capacity may be unavailable in the user's preferred home region at sign-up time ('out of host capacity').
Idle Always Free instances may be reclaimed after 7 days of <20% utilization; reprovisioning is possible but disruptive.
Arm CPU BGE-M3 encoder latency may exceed the proposed 2 s p95 gate (unmeasured).
Oracle free-tier terms (idle reclamation, capacity) can change.
No API server exists yet - building one is a separate future task.
limitations: This task did NOT provision infrastructure, deploy code, or change production defaults.
Encoder and generator latency were NOT measured in the target environment (it does not exist yet).
The profile is retrieval-only; it is not a complete AI assistant.
rollback: If Oracle capacity/eligibility fails: fall back to running retrieval locally on the existing VM (already validated) or re-evaluate HF Spaces / other profiles.
If encoder latency fails the gate on Arm: keep BM25-only as the production default (already the case) and treat hybrid as bench-only.
If idle reclamation disrupts service: implement a lightweight keep-alive or accept on-demand reprovisioning.
The feature flag (SVK_RETRIEVAL_MODE) rollback to bm25 is instant and lossless (Task-76 doc).
